summary: The note examines how quantum computing both threatens and could strengthen cybersecurity. Shor's algorithm could break public-key cryptography, so researchers are developing post-quantum cryptography (PQC), and organizations are urged to inventory their cryptographic systems, train quantum-aware staff, and adopt hybrid quantum-safe strategies. It cites expert comments from several 2023-2024 forums and describes the field as a race against time.
one_line: Overview of quantum computing's dual role in cybersecurity: threats to current encryption, post-quantum cryptography, workforce training, and quantum-safe strategies.
key_facts: The note is dated September 15, 2023, and covers the intersection of quantum computing and cybersecurity.
Qubits can exist in multiple states simultaneously through superposition, unlike classical bits that are 0 or 1.
Quantum entanglement links physically separate qubits so that the state of one instantly influences the state of another, regardless of distance.

Shor's algorithm, formulated by mathematician Peter Shor in the 1990s, could let quantum computers efficiently factor large numbers, undermining public-key cryptography that depends on this being difficult.

Dr. Rachel Lin of the Beijing Institute of Technology said at the Quantum Tech Forum on September 20, 2023: "Quantum computing is not just a futuristic concept—it's the present knocking on the door of the cybersecurity fortress."
Professor Johnathan Michaels said on October 3, 2023: "It's not a question of if but when quantum computers will be strong enough to crack our current encryption."

At CyberSecCon on November 12, 2023, Katherine Suarez, head of the Global Quantum Initiative, highlighted PQC candidates: lattice-based, hash-based, code-based, and multivariate polynomial cryptography.
NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) is among the international standards organizations considering PQC algorithms for widespread adoption.
Jacob Torres said at the CyberNext Summit on October 23, 2023 that a workforce fluent in quantum principles and PQC must be built, or a critical gap in defensive posture will remain.

Organizations are urged to inventory current cryptographic systems, identify vulnerabilities, and develop a roadmap for integrating PQC; QuantLock Corporation already offers quantum safety assessments.
The World Crypto Summit in Zurich on December 1, 2023 discussed a hybrid approach combining classical and quantum-resistant algorithms, plus forward secrecy and quantum key distribution (QKD).
SafeQuant Enterprises has run experiments using quantum random number generators to improve cryptographic key generation.
Gary Benton, CTO of SecureVirtual, said at the Quantum Safe Security Workshop on January 15, 2024 that defense mechanisms will become more complex and significantly more robust.
